column1: # One line per device tag and per engine, for scripts/readme-device-list.sh. The registry carries no
# description field, so these are written by hand, each condensed from the header comment of the device's
# own *_types.h. The script REFUSES to run when a registry device or engine has no line here, so a new
# device cannot silently drop out of the README. Format: <tag or engine:Name><TAB><one line>.

column2: Multimode filter: lowpass, bandpass, highpass and more, with drive, spread and morph.
Strips the fundamental with a note-tracking notch and puts a clean sine sub-harmonic back.
Three-band upward and downward compressor, with Character and Vibe zones.
Stutterer: eight slicing modes over one ring buffer, a perform circle, grain and post lanes.
Four filter states on a plane, and one Morph that walks between them.
A filter whose response is drawn: four frames blended on an XY pad.
Table waveshaper whose curve is a place in a φ-field rather than a preset.
The Automodulator: an auto-wah whose filter, comb and envelope response are read from one position in the φ-field.
Delay, attack, hold, decay, sustain, release envelope.
Multi-segment envelope: a shape made of segments you draw.
Pitch tracker: the held note's pitch as a modulation source, with a rule for which note of a chord it follows.
Note Expressions: seven per-note controllers (volume, pan, tune, vibrato, expression, brightness and more) as routable outputs.
Gain, pan, dual pan, width and polarity.
Chain: devices in series inside one slot, with its own macros and routes.
Low-frequency oscillator with shapes, sync, phase and its own preview.
Delay with Clean, Granular, Xfade, Tape, Multi-Tap, Reverse and Buckets modes, and an effects lane in its feedback loop.
Pitch shifter, with an option to lock to a scale.
A very short comb whose delay is shaken by filtered noise, then soft-clipped and folded.
Featherverb: an algorithmic reverb, extended with a convolution section.
Compressor, limiter and compander, with a lane between the compander's halves.
Clipper with five characters and 4x oversampling.
Scanned-string resonator: bowed and plucked notes plus a drone, with effects lanes for each.
Four macro knobs as a modulator device.
Combines two modulation inputs into one output, through a transfer curve.
Smooth Shaper: eight waveshapers behind one knob, and a Twist that sweeps four modifiers at once.
Parametric EQ for surgical and mastering work, with an analyser.
Disperser: a dispersion (allpass group-delay) effect.
Phaser and flanger, with a response view and an explore field.
Left/right modulation sources (split, width) for stereo routes.
Spectral effect: the Additive engine's partial operators applied to any audio.
Adds noise or pseudorandom impulses to whatever passes, through its own filter.
Random Trigger: pseudorandom events as modulation.
Sample & Hold, with a built-in noise source and a trigger threshold.
Step sequencer: up to 32 steps of value, gate, probability, ratchet and slew, with randomisation.
Envelope follower, and a threshold that turns any signal into trigger pulses.
Chains side by side, combined by mode (Parallel, Select/Blend, Mid/Side, Left/Right, Bands), each with level, mute and solo, plus eight macros.
Sidechain Inject: brings the plugin's sidechain input into the chain at this point.
Classic arpeggiator: makes notes from the held chord.
Pattern: a terrain arpeggiator with four patterns, fills and routable outputs.
Twin Field: eight modulation outputs read off the φ terrain in two crossfaded layers.
The original PhiMorph oscillator.
The original PhiStair oscillator.
The default engine.
A resonator engine: a string, bar, tube or membrane model.
Classic oscillator shapes.
Additive synthesis, with a spectrum panel of partial operators and a vocoder.
Plucked-string engine.
Eight-pad drum kit, with a hit picture per pad and a PAD FX rail.
